pages.title: Data transfer Instructions
pages.text:
Data transfer Instructions:

Move destination, source
Source can be register, memorylocation, immediate operand.
both can't be memory location at the same time

stack operations:
PUSH AX - POP AX - Pusha AX - PopA AX
AX can be any register or memory location

address transfer:
LEA register, source
LES BX, [DI] <-> mov BX, offset [DI]}
To Get the address of DI "first char" and store it in BX

Arithmetic Instructions:

- ADD destination, source
with add operation we can add byte to byte or word to word like:
ADD AX, CX
byte to word is wrong
8 bits  16 bits
I/ Carry flag CF!

- ADC AX, 15H -> AX = AX + 15H + 1 (since CF = 1)
- INC source: increase register or source by 1
if AX = 8 INC AX -> AX = 9
- AAA -> It correct the content of AL

For Subtraction:
- SUB Destination, source (Same as ADD)
SUB AX, 4H -> AX = AX - 4H
- DEC source: decrease source by 1
- NEG source: change the sign of the source (opposite sign)

pages.title: IT2207 - SBB, CMP, MUL & DIV Instructions
pages.text:
IT2207 (2) 16.5.2025

- SBB destination, source : Subtract with Borrow/carry
Like if the Carry Flag CF = 1 it decrement the answer by 1
ex: Mov AX, 12H } first we make AX = 12 H
SCF } this change the value of CF from 0 to 1
SBB AX, 5 } Subtract AX = AX - 5 - CF = 6H

- CMP destination, source : Compare two specific bytes or words and do an instruction according to the result
CMP AX, 7H } this compare AL with 7 by subtracting them from each other
JNZ end; -> if Not Zero jump to end.

for multiplication:
- MUL source: it multiply byte by byte or word by word.
1. if source is 1 byte then AL is multiplied by it and stored in AX
2. if source is word then AX is multiplied by it and stored in DX:AX (DX is upper) (AX is lower)

- IMUL source:
Same as Mul but it consider signs

for Division:
- DIV source: it divides word by byte or doubleword by word
if source is 1 byte, AX is divided by source and
quotient = AL & remainder = AH

pages.title: Division & Variable declaration
pages.text:
if source is 1 word, (DX:AX) is divided by source, and AX = quotient, DX = remainder.
- IDIV: is signed division instruction

Variable declaration in assembly:

DB: Define byte (8 bits); x db ? (uninitialized variable)
DW: Define word (16 bits) / Y DW 5, Y = 5
DD: Define double word (32 bits)
DF: 48 bits
DQ: Define Quad word (64 bits)

Read/Input Variables:

To enter a character with the keyboard we do:
mov AH, 1 -> The function 1 is to read character
int 21H -> interrupt
The input is stored in AL. And the number is stored as a character to use it as a number:
sub AL, 48 OR sub AL, '0'

mov AH, 7 -> also we use this to read character but
int 21H -> it is not displayed in the terminal (character won't be entered)

Write or Display:

mov DL, 'A' -> you enter the character you want
mov AH, 2 -> to display to DL and then do this.
int 21H -> we can read only one digit at a time

Display a message:

mov DX, offset variable or Lea DX, variable
mov ah, 9 -> to display a message
int 21H

pages.title: IT2207 - If, else condition & Logical instructions
pages.text:
IT2207 (3) 17.5.2025

If, else condition:

we use cmp to achieve if-else in assembly
cmp source, destination -> to get the result of cmp then
Jxy address of Lable -> jump to address of Lable
jl: jump if less, jle: jump if less or equal, je: jump if equal
jne: jump if not equal, jg: jump if greater, jge: jump if greater or equal, jnz: jump if not equal zero, jz: jump if equal zero

If we need to use jump without any condition we use jmp address of Lable

Logical instructions:

- Not source: convert all the bits in a byte or word ex. 00110110 -> 11001001

- And destination, source: do and operation over all bits
AH = 1001 1111, AL = 0000 1011
- OR destination, source: or operation on bits
- XOR destination, source: xor operation on bits
if you have trouble understanding this check page 5, week 3

Shift instruction:

- SHL destination, count (shift left)
it moves the most left bit to CF
AL = 10110110 -> SHL AL, 5
The left and add zero at the beginning and add the moved bit as CF

- SHR destination, count (shift right)
same as SHL but in the other direction

pages.title: Shift, Rotate & Loop Instructions
pages.text:
- SAR source, count (Shift Arithmetic right)
we add the new bit according to the sign of the number, if it is negative we add 1's else it add 0's
ex: AL = 10111001
SAR AL, 3 => AL = 11110111

- SAL destination, count (shift arithmetic left)
Same as SHL

Rotate instruction:

- RoL destination, count (Rotate Left)
it rotate the bits in a byte or word so the left bit become the right and it is also added to the CF
ex: AL = 10110111
RoL AL, 1 => AL = 01101111 CF=1

- RoR destination, count (Rotate right)
Same as RoL

- RCL destination, count (Rotate through Carry Left)
In this instruction the first left bit is stored in the CF and the previous CF is added as the first right bit
10011 -> CF=0
00110 -> CF=1
01101 -> CF=0

- RCR
Same as RCL

Loop

- for: cmp cl, 4
jg end_loop
add S, cl
inc cl
jmp for
end_loop:

- while: cmp si, 4
jg end_while
add S, si
inc si
jmp while
end_while:

- if... then (->): if p true then q should be true... "called implies"
- If and only if (<->): this is true when both p and q are the same either true or false

pages.title: Rules of inference & Resolution
pages.text:
branch is closed if there is x & ~x in the same route.

Rules of inference:

Modus Ponens (laws of detachment - mode that affirms):
if a conditional statement and its hypothesis are true then the conclusion must also be true
p -> q -> condition statement
p -> hypothesis
.: q -> conclusion

Important table page 76 (Rules of inference)

- Satisfiability (SAT) and Propositional resolution

p -> q
q -> r
-----
.: p -> r

Literal is: p or ~p
clause is: p or ~p or p \/ q \/ r ...
Conversion to clausal
- p \/ q -> {p, q}
- p /\ q -> {p}, {q}
the empty clause is unsatisfiable

Proof by refutation or contradiction:

T |= A iff T U {~A} is unsatisfiable
to prove that T logical consequence of A we should take the negation of the conclusion (~A) and prove that it leads to an empty clause.

How to prove

{p -> q, q -> r} |= p -> r?
1. Convert this to clausal:
p -> q => {~p, q}
q -> r => {~q, r}
~(p -> r) => {p}, {~r}
then number them:
and last derive them from each other

pages.title: IT2207 - Processor control instructions
pages.text:
IT2207 (4) 23.5.2025

Processor control instructions:

STC: Set Carry flag to 1
STD: Set direction flag to 1
STI: Set Interrupt flag to 1
CLC: clear Carry flag to 0
CLD: clear direction flag to 0
CLI: clear interrupt flag to 0
CMC: Complement CF

Note: JNC means if CF=0, JNS means if SF=0
SF: get the bit in the MSB after an operation (add-sub) so we can determine the sign of a number
PF: if the number of 1 bits is even then it is set to 1 if the number is odd then it is cleared to 0
AF: contain the carry but from the fourth bit to the fifth

Loop Instructions:

First we should define CX (count) the rate of repetition and then start the loop ex. for:
and the CX value will automatically decrease by 1 each loop without do od that manually

Do-While loop:

same as for but use do

Array:

A db 10 dup(0) -> create an array of 10 element and fill them with 0
A db 1, 2, 7, 6
A dw 2, 5, 12
only si & di can be used to indicate an element in array A[si], A[di]
to move to a new line when display use: new line db 10, 13, '$'
